entries.summary: # Infinite Brutality Reference Boards Use these as silhouette and settlement-logic references, not as maps to copy. entries.summary: # Droobiedoo Context Index Droobiedoo is a read-only context source for the Home Center MCP architecture. It does not run an MCP server and does not execute workspace mutations. ## Owner Roles - Droobiedoo stores workspace-level project context, skills, doctrine, generated reports, artifacts, provenance, and freshness metadata. - Home Center exposes the index through read-only `drive_operation` entries so existing MCP clients can search it without reinstalling a connector or adding a new server. - Simulation Frames remain Home Center's immutable evidence-backed context lane. Droobiedoo task packets follow the same bounded context-packet discipline, but the checked-in index is a lightweight local source rather than a Firestore frame. - She-Raw remains the runtime/default consultative voice. It can consume a Droobiedoo task-context packet, but it does not own or mutate Droobiedoo. - Comman

entries.summary: # Tanks For The Memories - Information Pressure Discovery Date: 2026-06-20 ## Trigger Original assumption: - commander camera - drone camera - voice commands Correction: The goal is not to simulate a modern drone operator. The goal is to simulate a WW2 platoon tank leader. Therefore the drone camera violates the fantasy. It solves the player's information problem instead of creating it. ## Core Principle The camera system should not be designed around visibility. The camera system should be designed around uncertainty. The player should constantly decide: > How much risk am I willing to accept to gain more information? ## Primary Pressure System Information Pressure. Not health. Not armor. Not ammunition. Information. The player usually does not know: - exact enemy locations - exact enemy strength - exact enemy composition - exact enemy intentions The player must acquire information. Inf
entries.title: Tanks For The Memories - Information Pressure Discovery

entries.summary: # Tanks For The Memories - Ledger Simulation Discovery Date: 2026-06-20 ## Core Problem How do we create a giant historical cause-and-effect simulation with persistent people, commanders, crews, politicians, units, and battlefield information without paying for live AI agents? ## Answer Do not simulate thinking. Simulate: - identity - beliefs - information - doctrine - memory - rules The result is agent-like behavior without LLM costs. ## The Key Discovery Not AI Agents. Ledger Simulation. The world is a giant historical ledger. Entities do not generate thoughts. Entities receive information. Entities update beliefs. Entities execute doctrine. Entities generate consequences. The ledger records everything. ## Static Identity Important NPCs are fixed. Examples: - Churchill - Eisenhower - Bradley - Montgomery - specific commanders - specific platoon leaders They are always themselves. Their

Droobiedoo is the memory and training layer. The goal is not merely to generate animations. entries.summary: # Kitchen Scheduler ## Purpose Sequence one-active-task kitchen plans and assign passive work to the right appliance. ## Responsibilities - Pick the primary heat engine. - Pick passive tasks that can run in parallel. - Decide what should wait until later. - Prefer a single active task whenever possible. ## Scheduling rules - Start with the longest lead item. - Use the air fryer for small crisp items when capacity fits. - Use the oven for volume, convection, broil, or multiple components. - Use the microwave only as a staging tool. - Use cast iron for fast browning or fond. - Do not run two attention-heavy tasks in parallel. ## Default sequence - prep - long lead item - main protein or second lead item - quick vegetable - sauce - finish ## Output shape Include: - primary appliance - passive parallel tasks - next check time - final finish step - cleanup note

entries.summary: # Meal Composer ## Purpose Turn ingredients into a family of meal options rather than a single recipe. ## Inputs - bounded ingredient sets, like chicken, potatoes, broccoli - unbounded flexible pantry prompts - restrictions such as cheap-only, high-protein, low-cleanup, or accessible-only ## Output shape Return at least: - 3 bounded variants when ingredients are fixed - 3 unbounded variants when flexibility is allowed - one best quick meal - one best crisp meal - one best saucy meal - one best one-pan meal - one best fallback meal ## Composition rules - Separate meal identity from mere seasoning swaps. - Vary method, flavor frame, finish, and texture target. - Keep ingredients common and easy to get unless the user asks otherwise. - Treat flavor frames as reusable modules: lemon herb, soy ginger, Dijon, paprika, curry, buffalo, garlic butter, tomato, sesame, barbecue. ## Example outputs

entries.summary: # Rule Miner ## Purpose Discover new kitchen-specific doctrines from corpus reading and kitchen experiments. ## Responsibilities - Extract repeated cooking patterns from recipes and meal-kit cards. - Record exceptions and confidence. - Promote high-confidence transforms into the shared rulebook. - Distinguish recipe facts from generalizable kitchen laws. ## Rule format Capture each rule as: - condition - action - reason - confidence - exceptions - examples ## What to mine - temperature targets - visual brownness thresholds - parboil and braise triggers - dry-before-browning conditions - finish-step patterns - cheap-food boosters - accessibility cues
entries.title: Rule Miner

entries.summary: # Subsistence Upgrader ## Purpose Improve cheap base foods and boxed meals without turning them into elaborate recipes. ## Jobs - Upgrade hamburger helper style meals. - Rescue bland, thin, or dry food. - Improve leftovers. - Add a few high-value boosters to cheap staples. ## Default booster stack - onion or garlic - tomato paste - bouillon or stock concentrate - Worcestershire or soy sauce - butter or oil - acid at the end - cheese, herbs, or crunch when appropriate ## Repair logic - Flat -> salt or umami - Thin -> reduction or starch - Dry -> fat or sauce - Heavy -> acid - Monotone -> crunch or freshness - Boxed -> one browned thing plus one finish ## Example uses - brown beef, add onion, tomato paste, bouillon, Worcestershire - rice with butter, bouillon, and a fried egg - beans with onion, garlic, paprika, and vinegar - pasta with tomato paste, garlic, cheese, and pasta water
entries.title: Subsistence Upgrader

entries.summary: # Example: Braise Decision ## Braise when - the cut is tough or collagen-rich - liquid can improve the result - leftovers matter - time is more available than attention ## Roast when - the cut is tender or evenly cut - browning matters more than tenderness rescue - you want passive cooking and lower cleanup ## Decision note If the ingredient is dense but not tough, par-cook then roast or fry.

entries.summary: # Example: Chicken, Potatoes, Broccoli ## Bounded variants - Lemon herb roast: chicken, parboiled potatoes, broccoli, parsley, lemon - Dijon pan meal: seared chicken, roasted potatoes, broccoli, butter, Dijon - Soy ginger bowl: chicken, air-fried potatoes, microwaved broccoli, scallion, sesame ## Orchestration - Parboil potatoes for about 10 minutes. - Start the chicken while potatoes dry. - Roast, air-fry, or skillet-finish potatoes. - Add broccoli late or stage it in the microwave if frozen. - Finish with acid, herbs, or sauce.

entries.summary: # Example: Hamburger Helper Upgrade ## Goal Make a boxed or low-cost beef helper taste deeper and more complete. ## Upgrade stack - brown onion - brown beef - cook tomato paste in the fat - add bouillon and Worcestershire - add water or milk as needed - finish with butter, cheese, or herbs ## Output goal The result should feel savory, cohesive, and not watery.
entries.title: Example: Hamburger Helper Upgrade
